title: Priority heatmap and routing simulator for security & compliance requests
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Our current intake pipeline for security and compliance asks is manual, inconsistent across customers, and causes misrouting that delays responses for high-impact enterprise customers. We need a reproducible way to evaluate incoming requests (SOC2/ISO, HIPAA, GDPR/DPA, vendor questionnaires) and to simulate routing outcomes, team load, and SLA compliance before committing automation rules into production.

Goal: Build a Priority Heatmap + Routing Simulator that consumes intake metadata, scores requests by configurable rules, visualizes a heatmap of priority vs. complexity, and simulates how different routing policies affect SLA attainment and team load. This will enable PMs, Security, and Support to iterate on prioritization rules and thresholds safely and to provide predictable SLAs to customers.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator ingests anonymized historical intake CSV and produces a priority score for each row using configurable weights
UI heatmap view that shows distribution of requests by priority and complexity with filterable dimensions (region, product, request type)
Policy-simulator supports at least three routing policies (cost-based, SLA-first, specialist-first) and outputs projected SLA miss rate and queue impact
Exportable simulation report (CSV + PDF) with recommended threshold changes and expected monthly effort delta per team
Integration hooks documented: webhook spec for intake form, mapping to Linear keys, and optional Zendesk routing rule examples
Audit log of configuration changes stored for compliance reviews and exportable to Confluence/Drive
design_decisions: Score model will be rule-based (weighted attributes) instead of ML for explainability to legal and auditors
Complexity axis will combine questionnaire length, required evidence artifacts, and cross-team dependencies
Simulator output will provide conservative (pessimistic) and optimistic SLA projections to bound expectations
UI will be a Console beta view (read-only for non-admins) with export and save-as-policy features
progress_updates: 2025-02-18: Kickoff with Security, Support, and Infra. Agreed weight candidates and initial attributes list (sensitivity, customer tier, jurisdiction, artifact count). Confluence doc: https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENT/pages/79612/Priority+Heatmap+Kickoff

2025-02-22: Data engineering pulled 6 months of anonymized intake data (s3://redwood-prod/intakes/2024-08-2025-01) and provided sample CSV to the PM. Data quality note: 12% of rows missing 'jurisdiction' field; will add imputation step.

2025-02-26: Engineering spike completed (ENG-18811) — basic scoring engine implemented in Python with pluggable weight config. Prototype CLI repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/intake-simulator/pull/12

2025-03-01: Design (DES-11244) delivered heatmap mockups and an interactive filter spec. Design feedback: prefer small-multiples for product lines instead of single combined heatmap. Drive mock: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1zAHeatmapMocks

2025-03-03: Cross-functional review: Security requested mandatory checkbox for 'GDPR DPA contains data residency constraints' to be a hard routing rule. Added to ruleset and labeled for security review.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overfitting thresholds to historical data that include manual reroutes. Mitigation: include a manual override flag and run A/B test on new routing rules for 4 weeks before full rollout
Risk: Exposing sensitive customer identifiers in simulator. Mitigation: anonymize PII at ingestion and enforce tokenized IDs in storage
Risk: Too many policy variants cause operational complexity. Mitigation: Limit shipping to 3 canonical policies and provide guardrails for creating new ones
open_questions: Which teams are allowed to change weight configs in production? (Security suggests admins only)
Do SLAs vary by customer tier or should thresholds be per-product? (Support Ops leaning toward tiered SLAs)
Should the simulator include cost estimates in USD for total engineering effort or keep effort in FTE-equivalents?
next_steps: Finalize weight defaults and hard rules by 2025-03-07 (action: Maya + Elena)
Finish dashboard prototype and link backend endpoints (action: Liam, estimate 3 pts)
Run simulator on last 6 months and produce baseline report for leadership (action: Data Eng, deliverable due 2025-03-14)
Plan a 2-week alpha with Support and Security to review simulated outcomes before automating any routing rules
